verdicts.quote: Default schedule: reminders at 3, 7 and 14 days after the due date ("offsets"), sent at 09:00 in the business timezone ... Pre-due reminders are not sent

it is not void, written off, draft or disputed ... A partial payment leaves the invoice in scope with the reduced balance. ... Out of scope (bounded domain rules): ... credit notes; refunds; payment-plan invoices.
verdicts.missing: Whether credited invoices and invoices on a payment plan stop or continue the reminder sequence; they are listed out of scope, which doesn't say how they behave.

verdicts.quote: The amount is the invoice's current balance at send time, not its original total.
can mark a customer "no reminders" ... its customer is opted out, the offset is recorded `skipped: paused` or `skipped: opted_out` ... Out of scope: customer self-service unsubscribe (G-3)
verdicts.missing: Whether existing do-not-contact or unsubscribed states on the customer are respected, and whether billing reminders are exempt from a marketing opt-out.

verdicts.quote: at most one reminder message is handed to the provider per (invoice, offset). The evaluator claims (invoice, offset) by atomically creating a reminder record in state `sending` with a lease before the provider call
The evaluator re-reads the invoice from the invoicing system immediately before claiming a send (R-6) and never uses a cached or earlier-run copy for the decision.
A transient provider failure (timeout, throttling, 5xx) leaves the record retryable ... up to 3 attempts in total (A-7) ... persistent trouble is visible to staff (R-8).
verdicts.missing: Escalation to a person: whether anyone is alerted or notified when sends keep failing or the provider is down, beyond records showing up in the history.

verdicts.quote: volume and provider rate limits are unknown, so no bound is invented. Required behaviour under throttling is fixed by R-7.AC5.
verdicts.missing: How a large batch is paced within the provider's rate limit; only the reaction to throttling responses is stated.

verdicts.quote: No retroactive reminders: when the feature is enabled, a reminder whose scheduled instant is earlier than the enabling instant is never sent
sent at 09:00 in the business timezone ... Out of scope (bounded domain rules): ... weekend or holiday avoidance (a reminder due on a Saturday is sent on that Saturday).
One locale for message text: English, dates as "March 11, 2027", amounts as "USD 1,200.00" (ISO currency code, thousands separator, two decimals).
a missing or syntactically invalid contact address yields no provider call and the record `skipped: no_recipient` ... A permanent rejection (address rejected) makes the record `failed` at once.
The reminder is an email to the invoice's single billing-contact address. ... Out of scope: ... multiple recipients.
verdicts.missing: Which contact is written to when the customer or invoice has more than one billing contact; the spec assumes there is only one.

verdicts.quote: for each invoice, staff can list reminder records: offset, scheduled instant (UTC), state, reason ... attempts, instant of last attempt, and the recipient address used.

Body ... contains in order: a greeting line, `Invoice: <number>`, `Amount due: USD <balance>`, `Due date: <Month D, YYYY>` ... Out of scope: payment link or instructions (G-6; none in the default message)
Staff who can edit invoices can configure, pause and view reminders, until a role model is known (G-7). ... Out of scope: ... manual "resend".
verdicts.missing: The role model is left open (G-7, A-12 is only a placeholder), and who may send a reminder by hand isn't stated.

verdicts.quote: enabled flag (default off, A-4) ... can mark a customer "no reminders" ... Out of scope: ... manual "resend".
verdicts.missing: Preview or dry run of what would be sent; nothing in the spec mentions it.

verdicts.quote: staff can list reminder records: offset, scheduled instant (UTC), state, reason (for `skipped` and `failed`)
verdicts.missing: Any view of upcoming reminders the system will send next; records only exist once an offset is due.

verdicts.quote: Unresolved bound (G-4); no number is invented. ... At most one message per invoice per run.
verdicts.missing: A numeric bound on how late a reminder may go out, or on total sending volume per run or day.
